headerBody: Indonesia: Tourist Scams documents 73 specific scams across Bali, Ubud, Yogyakarta, the Gili Islands and 8 more destinations — each verified against Indonesian police records (POLRI 110), the BPKN consumer agency, Bali Tourist Police bulletins, r/IndonesiaTravel reports, and verified local news. Not a recycled blog list.
quadHead: Four ways Indonesia catches tourists off guard.

quad.title: The Airport Fake-Grab
quad.tl: Men hold “Grab” signs inside Ngurah Rai arrivals and quote 300K–500K IDR for a Kuta ride the real app does for 60K–100K — the official pickup zone is 50m outside.

quad.title: The Malioboro Batik Gallery
quad.tl: A “today-only batik exhibition” tout walks you 10 minutes to a “gallery” selling Rp 3M–15M “silk art” that is cotton print worth Rp 200K–500K.

quad.title: The Fast-Boat Ticket
quad.tl: Lookalike “Eka Jaya” and “Gili Getaway” sites sell Rp 450K–700K fast-boat tickets that turn out fake or double-booked — the real seat is Rp 300K direct.

quad.title: The Scooter Checkpoint
quad.tl: A traffic checkpoint stops your scooter for a vague “violation,” quotes a 1M–2M IDR “official fine,” then suggests 200K–500K cash “to make it faster” — no receipt, no ticket.

body: Indonesia: Tourist Scams is part of the tabiji.ai Travel Safety Series. Every scam is documented against Indonesian sources — the National Police (POLRI 110), the National Emergency Call line (112), the BPKN consumer-protection agency, and Bali Tourist Police bulletins — plus r/IndonesiaTravel reports and verified local news. Sourced, not recycled.

73 specific scams across Bali, Ubud, Seminyak, Yogyakarta, Jakarta, the Gili Islands, Lombok and more. The exact scripts, the red flags that give them away, and the Bahasa Indonesia phrases that shut them down — written so you can show them on your phone.
Scams evolve, so the book is re-researched every year, and the current edition sits in your Kindle library. Built for the traveler who wants to move through Indonesia relaxed, not braced.
